issues.description: The solution implementation declares lecture attributes using snake_case names (e.g. lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students) but the constructor, getters, setters and other methods use camelCase identifiers (e.g. lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents). This mismatch means the solution class will not compile and conflicts with the UML/problem statement which shows camelCase attribute names. This structural inconsistency between the solution and the specification will confuse students about the intended attribute names and prevent using the provided solution as a correct reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the field names in the solution match the UML and the rest of the code: rename snake_case fields to camelCase (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) and ensure the constructor and all methods reference those same fields. Alternatively, change constructor and method identifiers to match the declared field names, but prefer aligning fields to the UML/camelCase naming to avoid further confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) refers to attributes using camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). The solution implementation declares the fields using snake_case (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) while the rest of the solution's methods use camelCase names (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, etc.). This mismatch between the expected names in the problem statement and the field identifiers in the solution (and the internal inconsistency inside the solution) creates confusion for students mapping requirements to code and may cause compilation/runtime errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Use consistent camelCase attribute names across all artifacts to match the UML and getters/setters: rename the solution's snake_case fields to lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, and numberOfTutors (or update all usages to the declared snake_case names). Prefer aligning the solution fields with the problem statement (camelCase) so students can directly map requirements to implementation.
